english_text: It is important to understand your medical condition.
Knowing about your illness helps you manage it better.
You have the right to ask your doctor questions about your health.
You have the right to receive clear information about your diagnosis.
You have the right to be involved in decisions about your treatment.
You have the right to refuse treatment after being fully informed.
You have the right to confidentiality about your health information.
Your medical information cannot be shared without your consent.
You have the right to access your own medical records.
You have the right to a second opinion from another doctor.
It is important to tell your doctor about all your symptoms.
Always tell your doctor about all the medications you are taking.
Tell your doctor about any traditional or herbal medicines you use.
Tell your doctor if you are allergic to any medication.
Always inform the nurse if your condition changes between visits.
It is important to attend all your scheduled medical appointments.
Missing appointments can delay your treatment and recovery.
Regular check-ups help detect health problems early.
Early detection of illness leads to better treatment outcomes.
Prevention is better than cure.
A healthy lifestyle reduces the risk of many diseases.
Regular physical activity improves your overall health.
A balanced diet supports your immune system and recovery.
Drinking enough water every day is important for your health.
Getting enough sleep helps your body heal and stay healthy.
Reducing stress improves your mental and physical health.
Avoiding alcohol reduces the risk of liver disease and other conditions.
Stopping smoking improves your lung health and overall wellbeing.
Maintaining a healthy weight reduces the risk of chronic diseases.
Regular hand washing prevents the spread of infections.
Good hygiene protects you and your family from illness.
Vaccinations protect you from serious and preventable diseases.
It is important to keep your vaccinations up to date.
Screening tests help detect diseases before symptoms appear.
Regular blood pressure checks can prevent heart disease and stroke.
Regular blood sugar checks help manage and prevent diabetes.
Regular cholesterol checks reduce the risk of heart disease.
Cancer screening saves lives through early detection.
Eye examinations help detect vision problems and other conditions.
Dental check-ups prevent tooth decay and gum disease.
Mental health is as important as physical health.
It is important to seek help if you are feeling depressed or anxious.
Talking about your feelings can improve your mental health.
Support from family and friends is important for recovery.
Community support groups can help you manage your condition.
Health education helps you make informed decisions about your health.
Understanding your medication helps you take it correctly.
Following your treatment plan improves your health outcomes.
Completing your full course of treatment prevents drug resistance.
Never share your medication with other people.
Never stop your medication without consulting your doctor.
Always take your medication at the same time every day.
Store your medication in a cool dry place away from sunlight.
Keep all medications out of reach of children.
Check the expiry date of your medication before taking it.
Dispose of expired medication safely and responsibly.
Report any side effects of your medication to the clinic.
Ask the pharmacist if you are unsure how to take your medication.
Read the information leaflet that comes with your medication.
Understanding your treatment empowers you to take control of your health.
Wash your hands with soap and water for at least twenty seconds.
Wash your hands before eating and after using the toilet.
Wash your hands after coughing or sneezing.
Wash your hands after touching animals or animal waste.
Wash your hands after handling raw meat or poultry.
Use an alcohol-based hand sanitiser when soap is not available.
Cover your mouth and nose when you cough or sneeze.
Use a tissue when you cough or sneeze and dispose of it immediately.
Avoid touching your face with unwashed hands.
Avoid sharing personal items such as towels and toothbrushes.
Keep your home clean and well ventilated.
Open windows to allow fresh air into your home.
Clean and disinfect frequently touched surfaces regularly.
Wash your clothes and bedding regularly.
Bathe or shower every day to maintain personal hygiene.
Brush your teeth at least twice a day.
Use clean and safe drinking water at all times.
Boil water if you are unsure whether it is safe to drink.
Store drinking water in a clean covered container.
Wash fruits and vegetables before eating them.
Cook meat and poultry thoroughly before eating.
Avoid eating food that has been left out for more than two hours.
Refrigerate leftovers promptly to prevent food poisoning.
Avoid sharing food or drinks with someone who is sick.
Stay at home when you are sick to prevent spreading illness.
Wear a mask if you have a respiratory illness.
Dispose of waste properly to prevent the spread of disease.
Use a toilet or latrine and do not defecate in the open.
Wash your hands after using the toilet or latrine.
Keep your toilet or latrine clean and covered.
Use insect repellent to protect against mosquito bites.
Sleep under a mosquito net to prevent malaria.
Wear long sleeves and trousers in areas with many mosquitoes.
Remove standing water around your home to prevent mosquito breeding.
Wear shoes to protect your feet from soil-transmitted infections.
Avoid walking barefoot in areas with animal waste.
Protect your skin from cuts and wounds to prevent infection.
Clean and cover all wounds immediately to prevent infection.
Seek medical attention for wounds that do not heal.
Avoid contact with the blood or body fluids of other people.
Use gloves when handling blood or body fluids.
Dispose of sharp objects safely to prevent needle-stick injuries.
Do not reuse syringes or needles.
Use condoms consistently to prevent sexually transmitted infections.
Get tested for sexually transmitted infections regularly.
Inform your sexual partner if you have a sexually transmitted infection.
Seek treatment for sexually transmitted infections immediately.
Avoid sexual contact until your sexually transmitted infection is treated.
Reduce your number of sexual partners to lower your risk of infection.
Discuss your sexual health openly with your healthcare provider.
Do not stigmatise people living with infectious diseases.
Treat people with infectious diseases with dignity and respect.
Support family members and friends who are living with illness.
Encourage people in your community to seek medical care early.
Share health information with your family and community.
Attend community health education sessions at your local clinic.
Ask your community health worker for health advice and support.
Report disease outbreaks in your community to the health authorities.
Follow public health guidelines during disease outbreaks.
Cooperate with health workers during community health campaigns.
Eating a balanced diet is essential for good health.
A balanced diet includes foods from all the major food groups.
Eat plenty of fruits and vegetables every day.
Choose whole grains over refined grains for better nutrition.
Include protein-rich foods such as meat, fish, eggs, and legumes.
Eat dairy products or calcium-rich foods for strong bones.
Limit your intake of foods high in sugar and salt.
Avoid processed and fast foods as much as possible.
Cook with healthy oils such as olive oil or sunflower oil.
Avoid frying food and choose grilling or steaming instead.
Eat smaller portions more frequently throughout the day.
Do not skip meals especially breakfast.
Drink at least eight glasses of water every day.
Avoid sugary drinks such as cool drinks and fruit juices.
Limit your intake of caffeinated drinks such as tea and coffee.
Avoid alcohol or drink only in moderation.
Read food labels to understand what you are eating.
Choose foods that are low in saturated fat and cholesterol.
Increase your fibre intake by eating more vegetables and whole grains.
Fibre helps prevent constipation and reduces the risk of bowel cancer.
Iron-rich foods such as red meat and spinach prevent anaemia.
Vitamin C helps your body absorb iron from plant-based foods.
Folate-rich foods such as leafy greens are important during pregnancy.
Vitamin D from sunlight and food is important for bone health.
Calcium-rich foods such as milk and cheese strengthen your bones.
Zinc-rich foods support your immune system and wound healing.
Omega-3 fatty acids from fish support heart and brain health.
Antioxidant-rich foods protect your body from cell damage.
A healthy diet supports your immune system and helps fight infection.
Good nutrition speeds up recovery from illness.
Malnutrition weakens the immune system and increases the risk of infection.
Obesity increases the risk of diabetes, heart disease, and cancer.
Physical activity combined with a healthy diet helps maintain a healthy weight.
Avoid eating late at night to support healthy digestion.
Chew your food slowly and thoroughly for better digestion.
Eat in a calm environment without distractions.
Plan your meals in advance to make healthier food choices.
Prepare meals at home to control the ingredients and portions.
Involve your family in preparing healthy meals.
Teach your children about healthy eating from an early age.
Grow your own vegetables if possible to improve food security.
Access community food programmes if you are struggling to afford food.
Ask the clinic dietitian for personalised nutrition advice.
Follow the nutrition plan given to you by your healthcare provider.
Inform your doctor if you are struggling to afford nutritious food.
Social grants and food assistance programmes are available to those in need.
Good nutrition is a right and not a privilege.
A well-nourished body heals faster and fights disease better.
Nutrition and medication work together to improve your health.
Do not take your medication on an empty stomach unless instructed.
Some medications must be taken with food to reduce side effects.
Some medications must be taken on an empty stomach to be absorbed properly.
Ask your pharmacist about the best way to take your medication.
Certain foods can interact with your medication and reduce its effectiveness.
Grapefruit can interact with some medications and should be avoided.
Dairy products can reduce the absorption of some antibiotics.
High-fat meals can affect how some medications are absorbed.
Alcohol interacts with many medications and should be avoided.
Always inform your doctor about your diet when discussing your medication.
A healthy diet is one of the most powerful tools for managing your health.
Regular physical activity improves your heart health.
Exercise helps control blood sugar levels in people with diabetes.
Physical activity helps lower high blood pressure.
Exercise helps maintain a healthy weight.
Regular physical activity improves your mental health and mood.
Exercise reduces the risk of depression and anxiety.
Physical activity improves your sleep quality.
Exercise strengthens your muscles and bones.
Regular physical activity reduces the risk of falls in older adults.
Exercise improves your energy levels and reduces fatigue.
Physical activity boosts your immune system.
Exercise reduces the risk of heart disease and stroke.
Regular physical activity reduces the risk of certain cancers.
Exercise improves your flexibility and balance.
Physical activity helps manage chronic pain.
Aim for at least thirty minutes of moderate exercise most days.
Walking is a simple and effective form of physical activity.
Cycling, swimming, and dancing are all good forms of exercise.
Household chores and gardening also count as physical activity.
Start slowly and gradually increase the intensity of your exercise.
